solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Raise fewer arguments after convincing demonstration (6,6)

indicators.note: ON comes after the first phrase, and 'on' can itself mean after, as in 'later on'

blocks.note: to raise an objection is to object

annotation.surface: Someone learns to stop quibbling after being shown something that settles the argument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raise' is a verb about objections, not lifting; 'after' does double duty, meaning 'on' and placing that piece last.
annotation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a practical example that convincingly demonstrates a principle.

entries.clue: Keep returning unwrapped porcelain box (7)

indicators.note: going back the way it came: the letters are read in reverse
the wrapping, the outer letters, comes off

blocks.note: Sèvres porcelain, made at the French factory

annotation.surface: A collector keeps sending back a piece of china that arrived without its packing.
annotation.walkthrough: SEVRES and BOX run together as SEVRESBOX; unwrapping strips the outer S and X to leave EVRESBO, which reads OBSERVE backwards. 'Keep' is the verb, as in keeping or observing a rule.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of complying: you keep the Sabbath or a rule in the same way you observe it.

entries.clue: American Lord is mocking physical exercise drills (7)

indicators.note: PE bores into JEERS, as a drill goes into a wall

annotation.surface: An American aristocrat sneers at a keep-fit regime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lord' is the exclamation, as in 'Lord!', and 'Jeepers!' is its American equivalent. 'Drills' looks like a noun for the exercises; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Jeepers is a mild American exclamation of surprise, like 'Lord!'.

entries.clue: Disc that fastens to cycle snatched by phoney cleaner (6,3)

indicators.note: the letters go round: BU moves from the front to the back
COD grabs the cycled word and holds it inside

blocks.note: a BUTTON, cycled so BU goes to the end

annotation.surface: A fake cleaner has pinched a disc that fixes onto a bicycle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' reads as a bicycle in the surface; here it is an instruction to rotate BUTTON. COD for fake is a British usage, as in cod science.
annotation.definitionFit: A cotton bud is a swab on a stick for cleaning ears and other small spaces.

entries.clue: See promotional material a lot (5)

annotation.surface: Someone is told they will see a great deal of advertising.
annotation.walkthrough: LO is the old word for 'see!' or 'behold', a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British plural used as a quantity word, as in 'loads of time'.

entries.clue: Matter this woman put on report (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue SHE sits on top of BANG

blocks.note: the report of a gun is its bang

annotation.surface: An issue a particular woman has raised in her report.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Report' is a document in the surface and a loud noise in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A shebang is an affair or matter, as in 'the whole shebang'.

entries.clue: By 8 o’clock, let up cast to replace player (7)

definitions.note: Octuple is an adjective, eightfold; 'by 8' is the phrase for multiplying eightfold.

indicators.note: letters thrown into a new order
the anagram takes the place of the player inside O'CLOCK

blocks.note: a lock is a rugby forward; it comes out

annotation.surface: A theatre instruction: by eight in the evening, finish casting a replacement actor.
annotation.walkthrough: '8 o’clock' looks like a time, but the 8 belongs to the definition and O’CLOCK is raw material. The player is a rugby lock, not an actor.
annotation.definitionFit: Octuple means eightfold, multiplied by eight.

entries.clue: It’ll deflect water if turned off, so it’s said (12)

indicators.note: the words are to be heard, not read

annotation.surface: Something is supposed to divert water unless it has been switched off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned off' suggests a tap in a clue about water; it means bored.
annotation.definitionFit: A weatherboard is a sloping board fixed to shed rain away from a door or wall.

entries.clue: Most like a picnic meal, the rest of the afternoon free of shackles (7)

indicators.note: the shackles are the outside letters, which both words lose

blocks.note: FEAST without its outer F and T
SIESTA without its outer S and A

annotation.surface: An outing with a meal and an afternoon nap, with nothing to tie anyone down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picnic' is not food here: 'no picnic' means hard work, so most like a picnic is the easiest. 'Free of shackles' applies to both words.
annotation.definitionFit: A picnic is something easy, so what is most like one is the easiest.

entries.clue: A doubter, but not one initially coming clean (7)

indicators.note: 'but not' means 'except', so the doubter is taken without the letter that follows
the first letter of 'coming'

blocks.note: one letter C, the first of 'coming', is removed

annotation.surface: A sceptic who is not coming clean about what they think.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coming clean' reads as confessing, but 'clean' stands alone as the definition. SCEPTIC has two Cs, and 'one' says only one of them goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from bacteria, surgically clean.

entries.clue: On set of shelves put something one may have to bear weight of TV (5-7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the burden goes on top of the shelves
places the first piece in that position

blocks.clueFragment: something one may have to bear weight of
blocks.note: a cross to bear is a burden
a dresser is a kitchen cabinet with shelves

annotation.surface: Instructions for standing a heavy television on a shelf unit.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about a heavy television set; TV is the abbreviation for transvestite.
annotation.definitionFit: An abbreviation: TV stands for transvestite, someone who wears the clothes of the other sex.

entries.clue: Ring HQ about confiscating Resistance weapon (7)

indicators.note: 'about' as in 'about turn': the soldier faces the other way, so O DEPOT is read backwards
the result takes R and holds it

blocks.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
R is the physics symbol for resistance

annotation.surface: Someone phones headquarters about seizing the Resistance fighters' arms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' and 'weapon' paint a wartime underground, but R is just the physics symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater weapon.

entries.clue: Imposter dropping soft soap? (7)

blocks.note: a sham is a fraud or impostor
a dropping, as from a dog

annotation.surface: A fraud who gives up flattering people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropping soft soap' reads as giving up flattery; 'soft soap' is really the liquid kind, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a soft, liquid soap, the question mark flagging the literal reading of an idiom.

entries.clue: Real Madrid and Barcelona? Not for them the 1-1? (5)

indicators.note: these teams go without the word 'the', so it is removed

blocks.note: el is 'the' in Spanish, fitting for Spanish clubs

annotation.surface: A pundit says the two Spanish giants are never content with a draw.
annotation.walkthrough: '1-1' looks like a scoreline; it is betting odds. The Spanish 'the' comes out of ELEVENS because the teams are Spanish.
annotation.definitionFit: Bookmakers' language: a bet at 1-1 wins as much as the stake, and the British call those odds evens.

entries.clue: Gradually categorising Burns this way? (2,7)

blocks.note: burns are classed as first, second or third degree

annotation.surface: Someone works slowly through the poems of Robert Burns, sorting them.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Burns the Scottish poet; here they are injuries, classed as first-, second- or third-degree.
annotation.definitionFit: By degrees means gradually, one step at a time.

entries.clue: In doldrums after losing house, have to come out (4,5)

indicators.note: the doldrums once they have lost the house
the second piece goes inside the first

blocks.note: drum is British slang for a house or flat

annotation.surface: A struggling worker who has lost their home has to move out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Come out' is British for going on strike, and 'have' is 'own', not a helping verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To down tools is to stop work, to come out on strike.

entries.clue: Light during day charges pointer? (3,6)

indicators.note: IN D rushes into the dog's name

blocks.note: bow-wow, a child's word for a dog; a pointer is one

annotation.surface: A light that runs all day is running up electricity charges.
annotation.walkthrough: The pointer is a gundog, and the question mark flags a definition by example. 'Light' is an old word for a window.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: 'light' is an old architectural word for any window, and a bow window is a curved one.

entries.clue: Conflicts wear out nurses very much (7)

definitions.note: Conflicts is plural; warfare is a mass noun for them.

indicators.note: the letters of WEAR are put out of order
the rearranged word holds FAR as if cradling it

blocks.note: far = very much, as in far better

annotation.surface: Hostilities are wearing out the nurses badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wear out' looks like one verb; 'out' is its own anagram signal and 'nurses' is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A mass noun standing for the plural: warfare is the business of fighting wars, conflicts collectively.

entries.clue: Left abandoned, one naturally sticks with Trump’s state force (7)

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so the L is dropped from the word it belonged to

annotation.surface: A politician on the left sticks with the president's forces.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a political side, but it is just the letter to drop. 'State' is the whole country, not one of the fifty.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from physics: impetus is the momentum or driving force that keeps something moving.

entries.clue: Who dispatches present? (5)

blocks.note: one who offs, that is kills

annotation.surface: A question about who sends out a gift.
annotation.walkthrough: To off someone is slang for to kill them, so an offer is one who dispatches; 'dispatches' looks like posting a parcel.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb, to hold something out for acceptance, and a jokey noun, one who offs, or kills.

entries.clue: Busy, having to cancel opening, say: “May I?” (2,3,2)

indicators.note: the first letter is struck off
May is one example of a month

blocks.note: May is a MONTH, which loses its M

annotation.surface: A busy person, having to call off an opening night, asks permission.
annotation.walkthrough: 'May I?' looks like a polite request; it is a month and a pronoun.
annotation.definitionFit: On the go means busy, constantly active.

entries.clue: Perhaps Leeuwarder is enthralled by the Rev. Paisley? (7)

indicators.note: IS is held captive inside FR IAN

blocks.note: Fr = Father, a title for a clergyman
the Rev. Ian Paisley, Northern Irish preacher and politician

annotation.surface: A man from a Dutch city is spellbound by the Northern Irish preacher Ian Paisley.
annotation.walkthrough: Leeuwarden is the capital of Friesland in the Netherlands, so someone from there is an example of a Frisian.
annotation.definitionFit: A native of Leeuwarden, the Frisian capital, is a Frisian.

entries.clue: Suitable support found in Apple’s first operating system (7)

indicators.note: the support sits inside the other pieces
only the first letter of Apple

annotation.surface: A good piece of backing is built into Apple's original software.
annotation.walkthrough: The computing surface makes 'support' sound like tech help; it is a physical prop.
annotation.definitionFit: Apropos means fitting, suitable to the occasion.

entries.clue: Very fine cut on the ear (5)

indicators.note: as it strikes the ear, heard not seen

annotation.surface: A very neat haircut round the ear.
annotation.walkthrough: The haircut picture makes 'on the ear' look like where the cut is.
annotation.definitionFit: A textile sense: sheer describes gauzy cloth so fine it is see-through.

entries.clue: Some juicy gossip gripped parting garden visitors (7)

indicators.note: BIT splits the birds in two

annotation.surface: Delicious rumours seized upon as the garden guests say goodbye.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gripped' looks like the container word, but it is BIT; 'parting' does the containing.
annotation.definitionFit: Titbits are small tasty morsels of news or gossip.

entries.clue: Recruit Don’s neighbour to guard large amount (7)

indicators.note: DEE surrounds RAFT, standing guard round it

blocks.note: the rivers Don and Dee flow into the sea side by side at Aberdeen
a raft of = a large number of

annotation.surface: A new soldier is posted next to a university don to protect a large sum.
annotation.walkthrough: Don is a Scottish river, not a lecturer or a Mafia boss.
annotation.definitionFit: American usage: the draft is conscription, so a draftee is a recruit called up by it.

entries.clue: Indicate corruption of old Commonwealth realm (7)

blocks.note: Belize keeps the British monarch as head of state

annotation.surface: Pointing to graft in a former Commonwealth country.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is political corruption; the definition is textual, marking a passage in a manuscript as corrupt.
annotation.definitionFit: To obelize is to mark a word or passage with an obelus as spurious or corrupt.

entries.clue: I will not work for retiring food transporter (12)

indicators.note: going back: the whole string is read in reverse

blocks.note: in print 'I will not work' is set in italics: stressed

annotation.surface: A striker's slogan: I won't work for anyone who is stepping down.
annotation.walkthrough: The printed clue italicises 'I will not work', so the words are STRESSED; NO OP STRESSED read backwards is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A dessertspoon carries pudding to the mouth.
